naruto.title: Naruto the Movie: Ninja Clash in the Land of Snow
naruto.note: Narutopedia places it between episodes 101 and 102; it must come before Sasuke leaves the village.

naruto.title: Naruto the Movie: Legend of the Stone of Gelel
naruto.note: Set after Sasuke has left the village; some guides put it after episode 147 instead.

naruto.title: Naruto the Movie: Guardians of the Crescent Moon Kingdom
naruto.note: Fits anywhere in the late filler run; episode 196 matches its release window.

naruto.title: Naruto Shippuden the Movie
naruto.when: Non-canon; best after Shippuden episode 32 (end of the Kazekage Rescue arc)

naruto.title: Naruto Shippuden the Movie: Bonds
naruto.note: Sai is on Team Kakashi and Sasuke appears, so it belongs after the Tenchi Bridge arc.

naruto.title: Naruto Shippuden the Movie: The Will of Fire
naruto.note: Guides differ (after episode 120 or 126); Naruto already uses the Rasenshuriken.

naruto.title: Naruto Shippuden the Movie: The Lost Tower
naruto.when: Non-canon; best after Shippuden episode 143, before Pain's attack on the Leaf
naruto.note: Narutopedia says it is set after Jiraiya's death and before Pain's assault; guides pick different slots in that window (143 or 154).

naruto.title: Naruto the Movie: Blood Prison
naruto.note: Does not fit cleanly; other guides place it after episode 221.

naruto.title: Road to Ninja: Naruto the Movie
naruto.note: Kishimoto wrote the story, but Narutopedia notes it does not match the manga timeline past Naruto's stay on Island Turtle.

naruto.title: The Last: Naruto the Movie
naruto.note: Officially part of the story, billed as manga chapter 699.5; episodes 494-500 (Naruto's wedding) follow it.

naruto.title: Boruto: Naruto the Movie
naruto.when: After Boruto episode 50; Boruto episodes 51-66 retell the same story
naruto.note: Written by Kishimoto and adapted as manga chapters 1-10 and anime episodes 51-66 (Chunin Exams arc), so you can watch either version.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball: Curse of the Blood Rubies
dragon-ball.when: Alternate retelling of the first arc; watch after Dragon Ball episode 13 or skip
dragon-ball.note: Replaces the Emperor Pilaf saga (episodes 1-13); the Daizenshuu guide treats it as a different world from the TV show.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball: Sleeping Princess in Devil's Castle
dragon-ball.when: Non-canon alternate take on Dragon Ball episodes 14-18; best after episode 18
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu places it at the start of Goku and Krillin's training with Master Roshi but notes it conflicts with the show.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball: Mystical Adventure
dragon-ball.when: Doesn't fit the timeline (alternate world); watch any time after Dragon Ball episode 101
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu calls it a completely different world; episode 101 is our pick so that Tao Pai Pai, Tien and Chiaotzu are already introduced.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball: The Path to Power
dragon-ball.when: Doesn't fit the timeline (10th-anniversary remake); watch any time after Dragon Ball episode 67 or as a standalone
dragon-ball.note: Retells the first Dragon Ball hunt and the Red Ribbon Army story (episodes 1-67) in one film.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: Dead Zone
dragon-ball.when: After Dragon Ball episode 153, before Dragon Ball Z episode 1
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu places it after Goku and Chi-Chi's wedding and before Raditz arrives; Krillin meeting Gohan here clashes with the TV series.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: The World's Strongest
dragon-ball.when: Non-canon; best after DBZ episode 35 (between the Saiyan and Namek sagas)
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu dates it between the Vegeta fight and the trip to Namek, though Piccolo being alive does not match the show.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: The Tree of Might
dragon-ball.when: Doesn't fit the timeline; watch any time after DBZ episode 35
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu dates it to the Namek period, but everyone is on Earth and the dead fighters are alive, so it is a movie-only story.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: Lord Slug
dragon-ball.when: Doesn't fit the timeline; watch any time after DBZ episode 35
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu sets it before the final Frieza fight because Goku is not yet a true Super Saiyan, while noting Goku should be on Namek then.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: Cooler's Revenge
dragon-ball.when: Non-canon; best after DBZ episode 125 (end of the Trunks saga, before the Androids arrive)
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu places it in the three years between Future Trunks' warning and the Androids' arrival.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: Super Android 13!
dragon-ball.when: Non-canon (parallel world); best after DBZ episode 146, before Cell reaches his perfect form
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu sets it after Dr. Gero's death and before Perfect Cell, in a parallel world; episode 146 is where Goku wakes from the heart virus.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: The Return of Cooler
dragon-ball.when: During the 10-day wait for the Cell Games; best after DBZ episode 173 (before 175)
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu places it between the Cell Games announcement and their opening; Dende is already Earth's guardian (episode 172).

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: Broly - The Legendary Super Saiyan
dragon-ball.when: During the 10-day wait for the Cell Games; best after DBZ episode 173 (before 175)
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu sets it around the final showdown with Cell, before the Cell Games begin (episode 175).

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: Bojack Unbound
dragon-ball.when: After the Cell Games; best after DBZ episode 194
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu sets it several months after Cell's defeat, once Future Trunks has returned.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: Broly - Second Coming
dragon-ball.when: Non-canon; best after DBZ episode 209 (just before the 25th World Tournament)
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu sets it shortly before the 25th World Martial Arts Tournament (episodes 210-219); Videl and Goten can already fly.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: Bio-Broly
dragon-ball.when: Doesn't fit the timeline; watch any time after DBZ episode 219
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu places it after the 25th World Tournament, during the Majin Buu period, and calls it a movie-only story.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: Fusion Reborn
dragon-ball.when: Non-canon; best after DBZ episode 252, before Super Buu appears
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu sets it during the Majin Buu saga before Super Buu; Gohan's presence still clashes with the show.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: Wrath of the Dragon
dragon-ball.when: Non-canon; best after DBZ episode 287 (after Kid Buu is defeated)
dragon-ball.note: Daizenshuu sets it after Majin Buu's defeat once peace returns.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods
dragon-ball.when: After DBZ episode 287 (before the 10-year skip in 288); Dragon Ball Super episodes 1-15 retell it
dragon-ball.note: Toriyama-written and retold in Super's God of Destruction Beerus saga; Daima is also set before the skip, but its order relative to this film is not officially stated.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Z: Resurrection 'F'
dragon-ball.when: After Battle of Gods; Dragon Ball Super episodes 16-27 retell it
dragon-ball.note: Set months after Battle of Gods; retold with changes in Super's Golden Frieza saga, so after Super episode 15 is the alternative slot.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Super: Broly
dragon-ball.when: After Dragon Ball Super episode 131 (the Tournament of Power)
dragon-ball.note: Toriyama said it takes place after the Tournament of Power, where the Super anime ends.

dragon-ball.title: Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero
dragon-ball.when: After Dragon Ball Super: Broly (anime viewers: after Super episode 131)
dragon-ball.note: A sequel to Super: Broly; in the manga it follows the Granolah arc, which the anime has not adapted.

bleach.title: Bleach: Memories of Nobody
bleach.when: Non-canon; best after Bleach episode 109 (end of the Bount arc)
bleach.note: Fits between the Soul Society arc and the Arrancar arc; episodes 106-109 used footage from the film in their credits. Some guides say after 117 instead.

bleach.title: Bleach: The DiamondDust Rebellion
bleach.note: Guides place it anywhere after episode 125, once Ichigo can use his Hollow mask; it premiered between episodes 153 and 154.

bleach.title: Bleach: Fade to Black
bleach.when: Doesn't fit the timeline; watch any time after Bleach episode 127
bleach.note: No consensus slot: some guides use episode 125-127, others its release slot between episodes 198 and 199.

bleach.title: Bleach: Hell Verse
bleach.note: Episodes 298-299 set up the film, which opens during Ichigo's fight with Ulquiorra; Kubo supervised it, but it is not treated as canon.

one-piece.title: One Piece: The Movie
one-piece.when: Non-canon; best after episode 18 (between the Syrup Village and Baratie arcs)
one-piece.note: One Piece Wiki says its status quo fits the gap between Syrup Village and Baratie.

one-piece.title: Clockwork Island Adventure
one-piece.when: Non-canon; best after episode 53 (after Loguetown, before Warship Island)
one-piece.note: Zoro and Usopp have their Loguetown gear; One Piece Wiki says it could also sit just before Reverse Mountain (after episode 61).

one-piece.title: Chopper's Kingdom on the Island of Strange Animals
one-piece.when: Doesn't fit the timeline; watch any time after episode 130 (end of the Arabasta arc)
one-piece.note: Chopper is aboard but Vivi and Robin are absent, which One Piece Wiki says contradicts canon; some guides use episode 102 instead.

one-piece.title: Dead End Adventure
one-piece.when: Non-canon; best after episode 138 (between the Arabasta and Jaya arcs)
one-piece.note: Robin is aboard but the crew does not yet know their new bounties, so it falls between Arabasta and Jaya.

one-piece.title: The Cursed Holy Sword
one-piece.when: Non-canon; best after episode 195 (end of the Skypiea arc)
one-piece.note: One Piece Wiki places it after Skypiea because the crew knows their post-Arabasta bounties; some guides use episode 143 instead.

one-piece.title: Baron Omatsuri and the Secret Island
one-piece.when: Non-canon; best after episode 206, any time before Water 7 (episode 229)
one-piece.note: Robin and the Going Merry place it between Skypiea and Water 7; guides pick episode 206 or 224.

one-piece.title: The Giant Mechanical Soldier of Karakuri Castle
one-piece.when: Non-canon; best after episode 228 (just before the Water 7 arc)
one-piece.note: One Piece Wiki sets it before the Water 7 arc.

one-piece.title: One Piece Film: Strong World
one-piece.when: Non-canon; best after episode 381 (between Thriller Bark and Sabaody)
one-piece.note: Story by Oda, but the film itself is not canon (its villain Shiki is); filler episodes 426-429 are its prequel.

one-piece.title: One Piece Film: Z
one-piece.when: Non-canon; best after episode 578 (after the Z's Ambition episodes, before Punk Hazard)
one-piece.note: First post-timeskip film; filler episodes 575-578 lead into it.

one-piece.title: One Piece Film: Gold
one-piece.when: Non-canon; best after episode 750 (between Dressrosa and Zou)
one-piece.note: Set after Dressrosa and before Zou; filler episodes 747-750 (Silver Mine) lead into it.

one-piece.title: One Piece: Stampede
one-piece.when: Non-canon; best after episode 889 (after Levely, before Wano)
one-piece.note: Luffy has his post-Levely bounty and the Warlord system still exists, so it sits just before Wano; the Cidre Guild filler episodes tie in.

one-piece.title: One Piece Film: Red
one-piece.when: Non-canon; best after episode 1085 (after the Wano arc)
one-piece.note: One Piece Wiki places it after Wano because Jinbe is aboard and Luffy uses Gear 5; episodes 1029-1030 (Uta's Past) are a prequel, which is why many guides list it after episode 1030.
